title: Self-driving Tesla crashes into highway patrol car, injures two officers
source_used: CBS News Sacramento (full text); ABC pool link is a video page with no text
key_facts: The crash happened late on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 on eastbound Interstate 80 west of Air Base Parkway near Fairfield, California.

The California Highway Patrol (CHP) said four lanes had been closed with flares and cones when the Tesla drove into the closure at freeway speed and hit a Dodge Charger patrol car with two officers inside.
Investigators said the 22-year-old driver from Sacramento told them he had been asleep and that the Tesla was in Full Self-Driving mode.
CHP stressed that Full Self-Driving is a driver-assistance feature that requires the driver to stay alert and in control.
CHP released dashcam video of the impact on Thursday 15 Oct 2026.
Both officers were seriously injured but are recovering; the driver had minor injuries.
The officers were investigating a separate crash about an hour earlier that killed a 19-year-old man from San Pablo.
quote_evidence: Investigators said the 22-year-old driver from Sacramento told them he had been asleep and that the Tesla was operating in Full Self-Driving mode at the time.
CHP noted that despite its name, Tesla's Full Self-Driving system is a driver-assistance feature that requires the driver to remain alert and in control.
Both officers suffered serious injuries but are recovering.
why_it_matters_hint: The crash puts Tesla's driver-assistance system and driver responsibility back in the spotlight, though the claim that it was switched on comes from the driver.
